To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the chemical freeze-out points are not the same as the hadrochemical equilibrium ones; (b) the difference between them is caused by hadronic interactions after hadronization but before chemical freeze-out; (c) the hadrochemical equilbrium points are very close to the parton-hadrion phase boundary predicted by lattice quantum chomodynamics; (d) this is the first experimental evidence that the QCD phase transition is of a first order nature.

1. the hadrochemical equilibrium in the (T,μB) plane is reached at the parton-hhadron phase boundary predicted by lattice QCD and 2. the chemical freeze-out in the (TμB) plane occurs at a significantly higher temperature and baryochemical potential than hadrochemical equilibrium

the observed hadronic multiplicities in relativistic heavy-ion collisions can be reproduced only after taking into account the hadronic rescattering effects and that the hadrochemical freeze-out points reconstructed in this way are consistent with the QCD phase boundary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the hadron formation process in the relativistic nuclear collisions at high energies.
the search for the phase boundary between the hadronic and partonic phases of the QCD phase transition and the determination of the critical point in the phase diagram of QCD.
the study of the properties of the strongly interacting matter produced in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed hadrochemical freeze-out is not the chemical equilibrium but the chemical freeze-out point, and the latter is located close to the parton-hhadron phase boundary in the (T, μ(B)) plane.

the chemical freeze-out points in the (μB, T) plane are consistent with the QCD phase transition and the hadron formation is a two-step process: first the parton-hydrodynamical phase and then the hadrochemical freeze-out.
the chemical freeze-out points are not the points of the QCD phase boundary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hadronic interactions after hadronization are essential to describe the hadronic multiplicities in ultrarelativistc nuclear collisions.
hadron formation in ultrarelatistic nuclear collisions occurs in the vicinity of the phase boundary between the partonic and hadronic phases.
the chemical freeze-out conditions in nuclear collisions are strongly influenced by the hadronic interactions after hadronization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hadronization process in relativistic heavy-ion collisions is not a sudden event but rather a process that lasts for a few fm/c and during this time, the hadrons produced in the hadronization stage are subject to inelastic reactions.
the hadronic interactions after hadronization are crucial for a proper understanding of the hadronization process in heavy-ion collisions and the phase structure of strongly interacting matter.
the chemical freeze-out points in the ( T, μ(B)) plane are not related to the hadrochemical equilibrium ones.
